about: CS-1239 clock goldens over the synthetic solve corpus. Every synthetic building declares an un-sharded clock base of 1.000000 = 1 (tests/solve/synthetic.py UNSHARDED_CLOCK_BASE_TEXT). The clamp limits to that base only when the requested clock is strictly above it; the ceiling is never known and the shard slot count is unmeasured (null) in the version pin.

cases.name: clamp_overclock_to_base
cases.why: 3/2 > 1, so the clock becomes the base 1 and the result says it clamped.

cases.name: clamp_a_hair_above_base
cases.why: 1.000001 is strictly above 1; an exact comparison clamps it where a float epsilon might not.

cases.name: clamp_at_base_is_not_clamped
cases.why: 1 is not above 1, so it passes through unclamped.

cases.name: clamp_underclock_passes_through
cases.why: 1/2 is below the base and is returned unchanged.

cases.name: clamp_zero_passes_through
cases.why: 0 is below the base; zero is a real clock and stays zero rather than absent.

cases.name: ceiling_is_unknown
cases.why: The base is the declared 1; the slot count is unmeasured, so known is false and no ceiling number exists.
